extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal financial assistance (K-12 schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and legal counsel implementing Title IX grievance procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how recipients must respond to reports and formal complaints of sexual harassment under Title IX, including the mandatory grievance process, supportive measures, scope of coverage, training, burdens, and procedural protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to investigate and adjudicate under §106.45 upon a formal complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: When a formal complaint is filed, a recipient is required to investigate and adjudicate in accordance with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised §106.44(b) and §106.45 to require recipients to follow the §106.45 grievance process for formal complaints. The grievance process is to be applied as a cohesive whole (see changes clarifying that the ten groups of provisions comprising §106.45 apply together).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide supportive measures to complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer supportive measures to a complainant in response to a complaint of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures must be offered even if the complainant does not file a formal complaint; providing supportive measures may bear on whether a court finds a recipient was deliberately indifferent. Recipients may provide supportive measures regardless of whether the alleged conduct is covered by Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education program or activity scope — substantial control test
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's 'education program or activity' includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes all operations of an institution (e.g., dormitories provided by the recipient, on- or off-campus). Incidents in off-campus locations (e.g., an off-campus apartment) may fall within Title IX if the recipient exercised substantial control over the context and alleged harasser; such determinations may be fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Title IX personnel about scope of program or activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide Title IX personnel with training about the scope of the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations revise §106.45(b)(1)(iii) to specifically require this training so recipients accurately identify situations that require a Title IX response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dismissal for Title IX jurisdiction does not preclude other disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: If alleged sexual harassment did not occur in the recipient's education program or activity, dismissal of a formal complaint for Title IX purposes does not preclude addressing the conduct under the recipient's code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(3) was revised to clarify this; recipients may also choose to provide supportive measures regardless of Title IX coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint requirement — complainant participating in program or activity
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'formal complaint' requires that the student be participating in or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity with which the formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No similar participation condition exists for reporting; changing classes or instructors does not necessarily mean a student is not participating or attempting to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.45 applies only to Title IX sexual harassment (not non-sexual-harassment sex discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 governs formal complaints alleging sexual harassment under Title IX; it does not apply to non-sexual-harassment sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints alleging non-sexual-harassment sex discrimination may be handled under the 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures recipients must adopt and publish pursuant to §106.8(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and protections in §106.45 apply throughout the entire grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures listed in §106.45 apply during investigation and throughout the entirety of the grievance process, not only during the investigative phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigation portion of §106.45 was revised to begin with the phrase 'When investigating a formal complaint, and throughout the grievance process, a recipient must...' to make this explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process grounded in due process and impartial fact-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45's provisions are grounded in principles of due process to promote equitable treatment of complainants and respondents and to ensure unbiased, impartial determinations based on relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes protection from bias based on sex, race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, or other characteristics and intends the process to reach reliable factual determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings against individual respondents (not groups) for Title IX determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX proceedings contemplate adjudication of responsibility for individual respondents; the Department declines to require applying §106.45 to groups or organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions against groups for conduct by members are disciplinary actions under a recipient's code of conduct and lie outside the Department's authority under Title IX; hence §106.45 is applied to individual responsibility determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to punish individuals who make false accusations under §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to punish individuals who make false accusations of sexual harassment under the §106.45 framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals who believe they were treated differently on the basis of sex may file complaints for handling under the 'prompt and equitable' grievance procedures in §106.8(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients retain flexibility and discretion in implementing §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the standardized §106.45 grievance process, recipients retain significant discretion over many implementation choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discretion includes: setting reasonable time frames for the grievance process; using employees or contractors as investigators/decision-makers; determining whether an advisor may actively participate; selecting the standard of evidence; choosing individual or panel decision-makers; offering informal resolution options; imposing disciplinary sanctions after a determination of responsibility; and selecting appeal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties' right to select advisors of choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must allow parties to select advisors of choice to assist throughout the grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While a party's advisor may be an attorney or not, the status of the advisor, the party's financial resources, or potential financial benefits to the recipient must not affect the recipient's compliance with §106.45. Recipients may limit advisor participation consistent with their chosen process, but must ensure fairness and equal opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient bears burden of proof and evidence collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient has the burden of proof and the obligation to collect sufficient evidence to reach a determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties also have equal opportunity (but not the burden) to gather and present witnesses and other evidence, review and challenge the evidence collected, and question parties and witnesses. This structure recognizes Title IX governs recipients, not parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process aims to produce accurate determinations and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 prescribes a grievance process focused on reaching accurate determinations regarding responsibility so victims receive remedies designed to restore or preserve equal access to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standardized framework promotes consistency, transparency, and predictability so enforcement does not vary needlessly among recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement without discrimination; Department retains enforcement role
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will enforce §106.45 and other Title IX regulations without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, or other characteristics, and will act as the arbiter of recipient compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department may enter voluntary resolution agreements (e.g., to require offering supportive measures). Compliance with the Department's regulations may affect court findings about deliberate indifference but does not substitute for all legal liability determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not import full court rules or constitutional criminal protections into §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to import comprehensive Federal Rules of Evidence, Civil Procedure, or Criminal Procedure, or constitutional protections unique to criminal proceedings into the §106.45 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some due process protections similar to court protections are provided where appropriate, the grievance process is designed as an administrative truth-seeking framework adapted for educational settings, not as a criminal or civil court proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic decisions and sanctions not prescribed by §106.45
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not address recipients' academic decisions (e.g., curricular matters or academic dismissals) and do not prescribe particular disciplinary sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients retain discretion to use disciplinary processes as educational tools; §106.45 focuses on procedures to determine responsibility and ensure remedies for denial of equal access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may address non-Title IX conduct under other codes but must apply §106.45 when conduct meets Title IX definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that do not meet the Title IX definition of 'sexual harassment' may be handled under other code of conduct provisions, but where a formal complaint alleges conduct that meets Title IX's definition, recipients must comply with §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarification (in §106.45(b)(3)) is intended to prevent circumventing Title IX requirements by processing true Title IX allegations outside the Title IX grievance process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to avoid bias and conflicts of interest in investigators and decision-makers
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.45 expressly prohibits bias and conflicts of interest and requires objective evaluators to reach determinations free from sex-based bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The grievance process includes protections such as requiring decision-makers to give reasons explaining their decisions; recipients must use investigators and decision-makers free from bias or conflicts of interest and implement §106.45 without regard to party characteristics.
